[English](llms-full.txt) | [Português Brasileiro](llms-full.pt-BR.txt)

# browser-automation-cli

> One-shot Chrome CDP automation CLI for AI agents with no daemon and no remote telemetry.

browser-automation-cli is a single-process Rust CLI that launches system Chrome or Chromium through CDP, executes agent browser actions, then finalizes and exits. Multi-step work must use `run --script` inside one process so `@eN` refs remain valid. Lifecycle: BORN, EXECUTE, FINALIZE, DIE.

Product settings are commands, flags, and XDG via `config path|init|show|set|get|list-keys` only. Logging uses `--verbose`/`--debug`/`-q` or `config set log_level`. Color uses `config set color true|false`. Chrome and Lighthouse use shell path or `config set chrome_path|lighthouse_path`.

## Command Surface (v0.1.9)
- Full inventory (**71** agent names via `commands --json`, sorted): assert, attr, audio, back, batch-scrape, click-at, commands, completions, config, console, cookie, crawl, devtools3p, dialog, doctor, drag, emulate, eval, exec, extension, extract, feed, fill-form, find-paths, forward, goto, grab, heap, hover, image, keys, lighthouse, locale, man, map, mitm, monitor, net, page, parse, perf, pick, press, print-pdf, qr, record, reload, resize, run, schema, scrape, screencast, scroll, search, select-option, sg-rewrite, sg-scan, sheet-write, sitemap, storage, submit, text, type, upload, version, video, view, wait, webmcp, workflow, write
- Note: `select-option`, `pick`, `submit`, and `storage` are agent inventory names (no longer documented as multi-step-only / omitted)
- Discovery: doctor (browsers_dir, lighthouse source, cache_redis, residual_disk + residual JSON ResidualDiskReport), commands, schema `<cmd>` or schema --cmd (goto/eval/type/scroll/assert/wait expanded), version, locale, man, completions
- Global flags: **57** long flags in the global help, being **55** product flags plus `--help` and `--version`; source of truth is `browser-automation-cli --help`
- Config XDG: config init|path|show|get|set|unset|list-keys
  - Important keys: dialog_settle_ms, chrome_path, lighthouse_path, openrouter_api_key, llm_base_url, llm_model, cache_backend, cache_redis_url, lang, log_level, stealth, stealth_profile, stealth_seed, browser_mode, input_profile, proxy_url, proxy_bypass, proxy_username, proxy_password, http2_enabled, robots_user_agent, scrape_no_cache — complete reference with all **217** keys in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`; machine-readable via `config list-keys --json`
  - `config unset <KEY>` restores a key to its built-in default and is the inverse of `set`; `config set <key> ""` is NOT the inverse, because for a string key it stores an empty value the normal path never produces and for a numeric key it is a parse error
- Stealth identity: stealth is ON by default; `--no-stealth` disables the anti-detection patches for this run; `--stealth-profile <PROFILE>` takes `auto`, `chrome-linux`, `chrome-win`, or `chrome-mac`; `--stealth-seed <SEED>` pins the identity across processes, so an N-URL crawl spread over N one-shot processes does not present itself as N different machines; XDG keys stealth, stealth_profile, stealth_seed, browser_mode
- Proxy: `--proxy <URL>` sets the outbound proxy for both Chrome and the HTTP engine and accepts `http`, `https`, and `socks5`; `--proxy-bypass <HOSTS>` lists the hosts that skip the proxy, in Chrome bypass-list syntax; XDG keys proxy_url, proxy_bypass, proxy_username, proxy_password
- Proxy credentials: `proxy_username` and `proxy_password` go in XDG ONLY, never in argv, because the process table exposes argv
- Human input pacing: `--input-profile <PROFILE>` takes `human` (default) or `direct`; `human` interpolates pointer trajectories, applies dwell between press and release, and paces typing; measured 2026-09-04 the human pacing cost grows superlinearly with the typed length (2281 ms for 1 char, 14236 ms for 2, 95781 ms for 4), so a long type can exhaust --timeout and return exit 124 — pass --input-profile direct for long fields; OPEN defect tracked in gaps.md; `--input-seed <SEED>` seeds the input jitter so a run is reproducible; XDG key input_profile
- Session shaping: `--warmup` and `--warmup-url <URL>` warm the session before navigating to the target URL; `--no-xvfb` skips the private virtual display on Linux
- Payload assertions: `--expect <EXPR>` asserts that the payload matches `key=value`, `key!=value`, or `key~substring`, is repeatable, and conjoins with AND; `--expect-exit-code` exits 65 when any `--expect` fails
- Navigate: goto (--init-script, --handle-before-unload accept|dismiss, --navigation-timeout-ms), back, forward, reload (CDP Page.reload + ignoreCache; init_script removed after nav)
- Local scrape/crawl/map/search/parse:
  - scrape --format/--formats text|markdown|html|rawHtml|links|metadata|screenshot|summary|product|branding|images|jsonld|json|feed|attributes (**15** live formats, CSV or repeatable multi-format; `raw-html` stays an accepted alias of `rawHtml`) --engine http|browser (browser applies formats via outerHTML; file:// + http → Usage; format/formats also in run scrape steps)
  - batch-scrape --urls-file --engine http|browser --concurrency, crawl --engine http|browser, map, search (cleans uddg= SERP redirects; the envelope carries serp_endpoint as known or unknown for the configured search_base_url, and zero surviving organic results fails with kind data instead of answering ok true with count 0), parse (PDF/DOCX/xlsx/ods + --redact-pii)
  - sitemap <url> is map with --sitemap-only fixed on: the DECLARED document, the robots.txt `Sitemap:` hints and nested `sitemapindex` descent, never a link-graph walk, so --depth has no meaning here; takes --limit, --include-path, --exclude-path, --include-subdomains, --ignore-query-params, --search, --sort, --dedup-key, --select
  - feed <url> is scrape --formats feed on the http engine over the RAW body (RSS, Atom, JSON Feed via feed-rs); selector and main-content reduction are HTML notions that would destroy the document, so those flags are absent rather than ignored, and Chrome is not offered because rendering a feed produces the browser XML viewer; takes --select, --header, --no-cache
- Interact: view (--allow-empty for blank about:blank), press, write, type, keys, wait (repeatable --text OR; CSS multi-selector OR; run url/url_contains/navigation/wait_timeout_ms), hover, drag, fill-form, select-option / pick (native select input+change events; HIG badge/popover / role=option), submit, upload, click-at
- Observe: extract (--llm/--question/--schema-json; XDG openrouter_api_key, llm_base_url, llm_model), text, scroll (run dy/dx aliases), attr (DOM property fallback), assert (url_contains/text_contains; kind console_empty / console_no_match), grab --path (formats png|jpeg|webp only; AVIF removed)
- PDF / monitor / utils (some without Chrome): print-pdf (CDP Page.printToPDF; one-shot + run; refuse blank without content), monitor check --url --baseline [--write-baseline], qr encode|decode, find-paths (--glob), sheet-write (CSV/JSON→XLSX), sg-scan, sg-rewrite
- Local media one-shot (path→path, no Chrome): image info|convert|resize|download|exif (re-encode strips EXIF; GPS omitted unless --include-gps), video info|download|convert|to-mp3|trim|thumbnail|manifest (HLS .m3u8 / DASH .mpd summarised without downloading media), audio info|download|convert|trim (ffprobe/ffmpeg optional via XDG ffmpeg_path)
- Tabs/Dialogs: page info|list|new|select|close|tab-id, cookie list|set|clear (clear requires --all), dialog accept|dismiss (--if-present soft path; `.data.dialog_settled`; XDG dialog_settle_ms; multi-tab session_id isolation with e2e gate), cookie, storage export|import
- Capture: console list|get|clear|dump (dump always writes valid JSON array `[]` when empty), net list|get
- Network observability: `net list` and `net get` only see traffic captured by `--capture-network` in the SAME process; `net list` takes --page-idx, --page-size, --resource-types, --include-preserved; `net get <IDX>` takes --request-path and --response-path
- MITM local one-shot: mitm status|list|get|har|export|domains|apis|init-ca|start|capture-url|graphql|ws|block|allow|redact (127.0.0.1 only; CA under XDG data; captures under XDG state)
- MITM cross-process bridge: `mitm capture-url <URL>` writes the capture and returns `data.capture_path`; `--capture-path <FILE>` then replays it in `mitm list|get|domains|apis|graphql|ws` and is the ONLY bridge between one-shot processes
- Global MITM flags: --mitm, --mitm-ca-dir, --mitm-har, --mitm-hosts, --mitm-ws, --mitm-max-body-bytes, --mitm-no-media-bodies, --mitm-redact-secrets
- --mitm-ws restates the default: WebSocket frames are always captured under --mitm, so passing it changes nothing
- Workflow journal: workflow run|resume|status (SQLite journal under XDG state)
- Advanced: eval, emulate, resize, perf start|stop|insight, lighthouse (flag→XDG lighthouse_path→PATH; binary_source real|mock; unit fixtures include chrome-captured LHR 13.4.1; e2e mock remains SKIP), screencast start|stop, heap take|close|compare|summary|details|class-nodes|dominators|dup-strings|edges|retainers|paths|object-details (needs --category-memory), extension list|install|reload|trigger|uninstall (needs --category-extensions; install and uninstall stay out of run), devtools3p list|exec (needs --category-third-party), webmcp list|exec (needs --category-webmcp)
- Multi-step: run (NDJSON or JSON array of steps; --json final envelope ok + steps[].data; --json-steps streams NDJSON per step; fail-fast may return partial data.steps; wait_timeout_ms; scrape format/formats), exec, record --url --path (--seconds default 30, --max-events default 200, first ceiling reached wins; writes page interactions as replayable `run --script` NDJSON)
- Multi-step stdin: `run --script -` reads NDJSON steps from stdin, one step per line, against a single live session
- Stdin mode is still one-shot: one BORN, one DIE, no daemon; the caller holds the session open while stdin stays open
- Stdin mode validates each line as it arrives and reports `validation: "per-line"`; file mode pre-flights the whole script before BORN
- Stdin mode keeps fail-fast: the first failing line stops the loop and the envelope carries the steps already executed
- Prefer stdin over shell process substitution: `run --script <(printf ...)` is rejected because the path lands in `/proc/<pid>/fd/<n>` outside the allowed roots
- Residual-zero disk hygiene (0.1.5 RES-01…12 still true): BORN auto-GC (`scavenge_stale_singleton_orphans` of `/tmp` org.chromium.Chromium.* Singleton-only dirs older than 60s); FINALIZE dual scavenge + re-scan of owned marker dirs (prefix `browser-automation-cli-chrome-`); never kills host Flatpak Chrome; doctor residual_disk + residual JSON fields scanned_roots, cli_marker_dirs, chromium_tmp_singleton_orphans, scavenge_safe_candidates, live_cli_marker_processes (legacy), sibling_live_processes, orphan_marker_dirs, foreign_root_orphans, ghost_marker_processes, process_table_unavailable; local scripts residual-check.sh / residual-stress.sh
- Intentional residual: GAP-022 ~53 transitive multi-version dups; GAP-023/024 PRD divergences registered
- Lifecycle: BORN, EXECUTE, FINALIZE scavenges owned Chromium /tmp orphans, DIE; product law residual-zero process + disk
- Lang: --lang pt-BR or config set lang localizes human suggestions
- e2e: 53 DevTools parity tools (PASS=52 SKIP=1 lighthouse mock contract-only)
- Clap: GlobalOpts Args+flatten; clap usage errors emit JSON when --json on argv; tests/clap_command_debug_assert.rs + parity_run_inventory

## Settings Contract
- Product settings: commands, flags, XDG via `config path|init|show|set|get|unset|list-keys` only
- Important keys: dialog_settle_ms, chrome_path, lighthouse_path, openrouter_api_key, llm_base_url, llm_model, cache_backend, cache_redis_url, lang, log_level, stealth, stealth_profile, stealth_seed, browser_mode, input_profile, proxy_url, proxy_bypass, proxy_username, proxy_password, http2_enabled, robots_user_agent, scrape_no_cache — discover complete reference with all **217** keys in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`; machine-readable via `config list-keys --json`
- Complete XDG surface, all **217** keys grouped by family. The source of truth is `config list-keys --json`, which also carries each default and description; this listing exists so a reader with no shell can still see the whole surface. Every one is set with `config set <key> <value>`, read with `config get <key>`, and restored to its built-in default with `config unset <key>`. There is no product environment variable: `PRIVACY.md` states that none is ever read
  - `audio_*` (4): audio_default_bitrate, audio_default_format, audio_download_max_bytes, audio_max_input_bytes
  - `browser_*` (3): browser_close_wait_secs, browser_mode, browser_scrape_max_body_bytes
  - `cache_*` (4): cache_backend, cache_max_resp_bulk_bytes, cache_max_resp_line_bytes, cache_redis_url
  - `capture_*` (1): capture_preserved_rings
  - `cdp_*` (8): cdp_connection_probe_timeout_secs, cdp_discovery_max_body_bytes, cdp_discovery_timeout_secs, cdp_event_broadcast_capacity, cdp_event_drain_poll_ms, cdp_network_idle_settle_ms, cdp_proxy_bypass_loopback, cdp_target_event_wait_ms

  - standalone (39): allowed_roots, artifacts_dir, color, dialog_settle_ms, dom_stable_window_ms, drag_move_gap_ms, drag_move_steps, encryption_key, eval_drain_slice_ms, event_pump_slice_ms, event_tracker_max_entries, extension_attach_poll_iters, extension_attach_poll_ms, ffmpeg_path, ffmpeg_timeout_secs, file_parse_cache_ttl_secs, gif_max_frames, ignore_robots, interact_settle_ms, lang, lighthouse_path, lighthouse_timeout_secs, manifest_max_bytes, manifest_max_variants, monitor_diff_max_bytes, namespace, nav_micro_settle_ms, network_idle_window_ms, openrouter_api_key, platform_child_poll_ms, platform_child_wait_secs, residual_orphan_min_age_secs, run_max_include_depth, screen, search_base_url, shutdown_deadline_secs, support_settle_ms, timeout, user_data_dir
- Restore a default: `config unset <KEY>`; `config set <key> ""` is NOT the inverse of `set`, because for a string key it stores an empty value the normal path never produces and for a numeric key it is a parse error
- Proxy credentials: `proxy_username` and `proxy_password` go in XDG ONLY, never in argv, because the process table exposes argv
- Encryption: `config set encryption_key` only
- Logging: `--verbose`/`--debug`/`-q` or `config set log_level` / `log_to_file`
- Color: `config set color true|false`
- Chrome / Lighthouse: shell path or `config set chrome_path` / `config set lighthouse_path` (plus lighthouse flag)
- Dialog settle: `config set dialog_settle_ms`; dialog accept|dismiss reports `.data.dialog_settled`; multi-tab isolation by session_id
- Cache Redis: `config set cache_backend redis` + `cache_redis_url` (`redis://` only; `rediss://` fail-closed); doctor `cache_redis`

## Contract Basics
- Success envelope: `{"schema_version":1,"ok":true,"data":...}`
- Error envelope with `--json`: `{"schema_version":1,"ok":false,"error":{...}}` (multi-step fail-fast may include partial `data.steps`)
- Clap usage errors with `--json` on argv also emit JSON error envelopes (GAP-002)
- `run --json` success includes `ok` and full `steps[].data` (GAP-020)
- `run --json-steps` streams one NDJSON line per step: `step`, `cmd`, `ok`, `result`
- Exit codes include 0, 2, 65, 66, 69, 70, 74, 78, 124, 130, 141, 255; the live `error.kind` enum is usage, data, no-input, unavailable, software, browser, protocol, timeout, cancelled, broken-pipe, config, io, so 255 is a fatal path NOT mapped by any `error.kind`
- Live schema fragments: `browser-automation-cli schema <name> --json` or `schema --cmd <name> --json`
